meta: Water leak sensors, auto shutoff valves and meter checks: what each catches and what it misses in Oakley, CA homes. Call (888) 910-8644 for a leak check.
lead: A water leak sensor in Oakley, CA is a small device that alarms when it touches water. It helps most near appliances, and it does nothing for a leak inside a wall or under a slab.
intro: A water leak sensor is a battery-powered probe that sits on the floor and sends an alert when moisture bridges its contacts. Some beep locally, some message your phone, and a few connect to a valve that closes the water supply on its own. In Oakley, CA, where you put one matters as much as which type you buy.
The sections below compare sensor types, show where to place them, explain what they cannot find, and give a simple meter test you can run without buying anything.

sections.h2: Sensor, shutoff valve or flow monitor: what each one does
paras: Three kinds of device get lumped together under one name. They protect against different failures, and they differ in how much they do once water appears.

sections.h2: Where a sensor earns its place
paras: Put them where a slow drip becomes damage before you notice. Water follows gravity and hides, so low points near fixtures work best.

items.d: Tanks fail by leaking at the base or from connections. A sensor in the drain pan or on the floor beside it gives early warning. If the sensor trips, our [[water-heater-repair|water heater repair]] page explains what a plumber looks at first.
Supply lines, stops and trap joints leak here often. A sensor at the back of the cabinet catches a drip that would otherwise soak the cabinet floor.
Supply hoses and drain connections take vibration for years. A sensor in the pan or on the floor behind the washer is worth the small cost.

items.t: By the dishwasher and fridge ice line
items.d: A cheap line to an ice maker can split without notice. Put one where the line enters the cabinet or sits behind the unit.
Wax ring failures and weeping supply lines soak the subfloor slowly. One next to the base catches both.

paras: A sensor only reacts where water touches it. A pipe leaking under a concrete slab, in a wall, or in the yard between the house and the meter can run for weeks without reaching any sensor. Sprinkler lines and irrigation valves outdoors are another common blind spot.

For those cases the signs are indirect: a bill that climbs, warm spots on a floor, the sound of water in a quiet house, or a damp patch in the lawn. If you suspect a hidden leak, [[leak-detection|leak detection]] with acoustic listening and pressure testing can pinpoint it without opening walls at random.
A shutoff valve added to the main is plumbing work under the California Plumbing Code, which rests on the UPC, so have a plumber install it.

sections.h2: A meter test you can run in ten minutes
paras: Turn off every tap, appliance and ice maker so nothing in the house is using water. Open the meter box and look at the small leak indicator, often a little triangle or dial, that spins when any flow passes. If it moves with everything off, water is going somewhere.

To narrow it down, close the main shutoff to the house and check again. If the indicator still moves, the leak is between the meter and the main valve. If it stops, the leak is inside the house, and you can start closing individual fixture stops to find the branch.

sections.h2: Choosing and maintaining what you buy
paras: Pick devices with replaceable batteries and a loud local alarm, since a phone alert fails if the Wi-Fi is down. Test them every few months by dipping the contacts in a damp cloth. An automatic shutoff valve belongs on the main line and should be installed by a plumber, because it ties into your supply piping.
Whatever you choose, know where your manual shutoff is. A sensor is a warning, and the shutoff is how you stop the loss.

localnote.h2: Meters, Diablo Water District and your side of the line
paras: A sensor only protects the owner's side, because the District keeps the mains and the line to the meter. The meter box therefore marks a practical dividing line for any leak hunt. Ask the district to confirm exactly where its responsibility ends at your property.

If your meter test shows flow and you cannot find the source, the district's phone at (925) 625-3798 is the number for reporting water emergencies. We serve homes throughout the Oakley [[service-area|service area]], and owners in [[plumber-brentwood-ca|Brentwood]] should contact the City of Brentwood for questions about their own utility. For a high bill that looks like a leak, record your meter readings first so the conversation starts with facts.

faqs.q: Do water leak sensors work on a slab foundation?
a: They work on the surface of the slab, so they catch leaks from fixtures and appliances above it. They do not detect a pipe leaking inside or under the concrete.
A meter test or professional listening gear is the right tool for slab leaks.

faqs.q: Is an automatic shutoff valve worth installing?
a: It makes sense if you travel often, have a finished area below the water heater or laundry, or want protection for a vacation home. It is a plumbing install, not a stick-on gadget.
Pair it with a sensor near the likeliest source, and test it as the maker directs.

faqs.q: How many sensors does a typical house need?
a: Think in terms of risk points: water heater, kitchen, each bathroom, laundry and any ice line. A small home may need five or six, a larger one more.
Cover the spots where a leak would cause the most damage first.

faqs.q: My water bill jumped but I see no leak. What now?
a: Run the meter test with all water off. If the indicator moves, close the main to see whether the leak is inside the house or outside.
Common culprits are a running toilet, an irrigation valve stuck open and a leak at the water heater connection.

faqs.q: Who do I call in Oakley if the leak is before the meter?
a: Diablo Water District handles the line up to the meter or backflow device, so call (925) 625-3798 to report it.
If the leak is after the meter, it is yours to repair, and a plumber can locate and fix it.

cta_mid: If the meter test says water is moving and nothing visible is leaking, a pinpoint check beats opening walls on a hunch.
cta_end: Book a leak check and learn where the water is going before it reaches your floors, with a clear price up front.
